summary: SF office: intermittent AP spectral interference causing VPN rekey failures and tunnel drops
description:
Issue summary: Multiple employees in the SF office report frequent VPN disconnects and re-auth loops during high-density periods (midday and late afternoon). Impact: Voice calls, screen shares, and CLI sessions over internal wireguard tunnels drop unexpectedly causing user productivity loss. Initial triage suggests wireless environment noise correlates with the events.

Observed client symptoms: VPN reports 'handshake timeout' or 'rekey failed', temporary RT latency spikes (200-800ms), and clients rebind to different APs during the window. The office has a mix of 802.11ac APs on 2.4GHz and 5GHz with 20/40/80MHz channels and dynamic channel selection enabled.

Business impact: ~12 users impacted intermittently; internal engineering standups and remote pairing sessions interrupted. No hosting/backend degradation outside office LAN observed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Be on corporate-employee SSID (wpa2-enterprise) in SF office during peak occupancy (11:30-14:30 or 15:30-17:00).
2) Establish long-lived WireGuard session to the corporate VPN. Start a large file transfer, voice call, or screen-share.
3) Observe for 5-15 minutes for handshake timeouts, rekey log entries, or sudden tunnel teardown.
4) Check AR/Client event logs on affected AP and central controller for channel change, noise, or deauth events.
logs: Client syslog (example): wireguard: wg0: handshake for peer 10.4.3.22: handshake_timeout
AP event: deauth frame from 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e due to co-channel interference; RSSI drop -62 -> -85 dBm
Controller: channel-selection triggered channel move on radio1 (ch36 -> ch149) due to perceived radar/energy spike
Switch logs: no CPU/port errors; uplink to firewall stable during event window
comments: Ava Thompson (reporter) 2026-03-10: Users report consistent disconnects while on calls; happens to different device types (macOS, Windows). Attaching a representative client syslog.

Ravi Patel (Network Eng) 2026-03-11: Initial look shows correlated channel changes on AP controller at the same timestamps as WG handshakes. Suspect DFS/radar-triggered channel moves causing short airtime starvation and client retransmits that break rekey windows.

Maya Lin (SRE) 2026-03-12: WireGuard config has default HandshakeTimeout set to 120s and Keepalive 25s; logs show handshake timeouts within 2-8s of large retransmit bursts — could be MTU/path-related or transient airtime loss. Suggest capturing pcap on AP during window.

Ravi Patel (Network Eng) 2026-03-13: Deployed temporary policy to pin high-density SSID radios to static channels (5GHz ch36/40) and disabled dynamic channel selection on two APs in the east wing. Asked front-line to monitor for new disconnects.

Support (notes) 2026-03-14: Users in east wing reported reduced drop rate after static channel pinning; central area still shows occasional drops. Next: schedule on-site scan for non-WiFi interferers and review AP firmware for reduce re-association acceleration settings.
investigation_notes: Correlation: Every WG handshake timeout aligns within +/- 10s of an AP channel move or a burst of deauthentication frames in controller events.

Hypothesis: DFS-triggered channel moves and adjacent-channel interference are creating micro-outages (<5s) that overlap with the WireGuard handshake/rekey window, causing sessions to fail to re-establish cleanly.
Alternative hypothesis: Some client NIC drivers aggressively roam and drop UDP flows during reassociation; combination of roaming + channel move increases probability of rekey failure.
Data collected: Controller event timestamps, per-AP noise floor graphs, three client pcap captures, WireGuard logs from affected hosts, and AP firmware versions (all on 8.5.x).
resolution: Workaround implemented: pinned critical SSID radios in the busiest zones to fixed 5GHz channels and temporarily disabled DFS on two APs; added client-side Keepalive tweak advisory for sensitive apps. Long-term: schedule RF site survey, replace a failing AP (reported elevated noise figures), and upgrade AP fleet to 8.6.x to pick up stability fixes for channel-change handling. Monitoring to continue for 72 hours post-change.
next_steps: 3) Fleet firmware upgrade to 8.6.x in canary group next week
4) Update runbook: add WireGuard rekey thresholds and recommend Keepalive tuning for office Wi-Fi
